content:
A valid certificate would disprove the complex Jacobian conjecture in dimension three. Indeed, for
\[
F\in \mathbb C[x_1,x_2,x_3]^3,\qquad \det J_F\in\mathbb C^\times,
\]
injectivity of \(F\) is precisely Keller’s Jacobian conjecture. The degree bound \(\deg F_i\le 6\) does not provide an exception.

Thus two distinct algebraic points \(p,q\) with \(F(p)=F(q)\) would constitute a negative solution to a major open problem. No such polynomial map is known in any complex dimension, so a genuine `map_collision` certificate cannot be supplied.
